notes.meaning: God finished creating the heavens, the earth, and everything in them. All created things were marshaled into place in perfect harmony like an orderly army. Creation was now complete, showing God's power and wisdom in bringing His work to an orderly end.

God finished His work and rested on the seventh day. He did not rest because He was tired, but because His work was done and He was delighted with all that He had made. His rest sets an example for us to pause from our daily work.

God blessed the seventh day and made it holy because He rested on it from His creative work. Making the day holy means setting it apart from ordinary days to be dedicated to God. He gave this day of rest so people in all generations could worship their Creator and enjoy His peace.

Here begins the detailed history of the heavens and the earth after they were made. For the first time, God is called the LORD, which translates His sacred personal name, Yahweh. Using this name shows that the mighty Creator is the same covenant God who relates personally to human beings.

Cultivated plants and field crops had not yet sprouted across the land. This was because God had not yet sent rain and there was no human being to farm the soil. Instead, water rose up as mist or springs to moisten the whole ground and keep it ready for life.

The Lord God formed man's physical body from the dust of the ground and breathed the breath of life into his nostrils. This direct breath from God gave man life and made him a living person. Our humble beginning from dust reminds us not to be proud, while God's breath shows how precious each human life is to Him.

differ.view: The living soul refers to an immaterial and immortal soul that is distinct from the physical body.
The phrase living soul refers only to physical life, while man's dignity comes from God directly breathing into him.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some scholars compare the account of man being shaped from dust to ancient stories like the Greek myth of Prometheus or Babylonian tales of humans made from clay.

notes.meaning: The Lord God planted a special garden in Eden, toward the east, and placed the newly formed man there. The name Eden means delight, showing that God gave man a home filled with beauty and joy. Everything Adam needed for a peaceful and happy life was provided freely by God.

God made all kinds of trees grow in the garden that were lovely to look at and good for food. In the middle stood the tree of life, which represented eternal life and fellowship with God. Next to it was the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, which served as a test of man's obedience.

A river flowed out of Eden to water the entire garden and keep it fertile and green. From there it separated into four distinct river streams. This abundant supply of fresh water showed how generously God nourished the home He made for man.

The first river was named Pishon, and it wound through the land of Havilah. That country was rich in pure gold, valuable aromatic resin or pearls, and precious onyx stones. Even with all those earthly riches, the greatest treasure was living in God's peaceful presence in Eden.

The second river was called Gihon, flowing around Cush, while the third was the Hiddekel, known today as the Tigris, running east of Assyria. The fourth river was the well-known Euphrates. Mentioning these real geographical landmarks shows that Eden was a real, historical place on earth.

The Lord God placed Adam in the garden to tend it and take care of it. Even before sin entered the world, God gave man work to do, showing that honest labor is good and satisfying. Taking good care of what God entrusts to us is one way we honor Him.

God generously told Adam he could eat the fruit from any tree in the garden, with only one exception. He commanded him not to eat from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, warning that eating it would bring death. This command served as a simple test to see if Adam would obey and trust his Maker.

differ.view: God entered into a covenant of works with Adam, promising life for perfect obedience and warning of death for disobedience.
The prohibition was primarily a test of moral freedom, allowing Adam to choose love and obedience freely rather than by force.

notes.meaning: The Lord God declared that it was not good for man to live all alone. He decided to make a suitable helper for Adam who would correspond to him and be his partner. God designed human beings to live in loving community rather than in loneliness.

God brought the land animals and birds He had created to Adam to see what he would call them. Naming the animals showed that Adam had authority over them and possessed great wisdom from God. Whatever name Adam gave to each creature became its name.

Adam gave names to all the livestock, birds, and wild beasts. As he studied them, he saw that none of the animals could be an equal partner or match for him. This helped Adam see his own need for a companion who shared his human nature.

God put Adam into a deep sleep so he would not feel any pain. While he slept, the Lord took one of his ribs and closed up the open spot with flesh. God used a part of Adam's own side to make the partner he needed.

God shaped the rib taken from Adam into a woman and personally brought her to him. She was not made from his head to rule him, nor from his feet to be trampled on, but from his side to stand beside him as an equal. In doing this, God Himself founded marriage as a sacred relationship.

Adam was filled with joy when he saw her and declared that she was bone of his bones and flesh of his flesh. He called her woman because she was taken out of man, recognizing her as his true equal. God gave him a lifelong companion to love and cherish.

God established that a man leaves his father and mother to be united to his wife, and the two become one flesh. Marriage creates a new family bond that is even closer and more binding than the relationship between parents and children. God designed marriage to be a permanent, loving union between one husband and one wife.

Adam and his wife were both naked, but they felt no shame. Because sin had not yet entered the world, their minds and hearts were completely pure and innocent. Where there is no guilt or sin before God, there is nothing to hide or be ashamed of.
